_comment: R32 for track V: one single-edit mutant per invariant the V1 cases claim, each with the case names that must catch it on an assertion. Run with `node tests/v/run-mutants.mjs`. A survivor, a stale `find`, a declared case that dies by exception, or an all-cases failure fails the run. The three the brief names — filter allowlist, stale-response guard, availability mapping — are ALLOW-*/SIZE-*/CURSOR-*, STALE-*, and AVAIL-*.

mutants.note: a filter value outside its vocabulary is accepted instead of refused
mutants.find: if ((allowed as readonly string[]).includes(value)) return value as T;
cases: V1-Q02 a filter value outside its vocabulary is refused and the default stands
V1-Q03 `off` is not a list filter, and the refusal says where those requests are

mutants.note: `off` becomes a list filter, so off-mode requests look like an empty result
cases: V1-Q03 `off` is not a list filter, and the refusal says where those requests are

mutants.note: a key id from outside the organization is forwarded to the service
cases: V1-Q04 a key filter must name one of this organization's keys

mutants.note: an unrecognised parameter is swallowed instead of reported
cases: V1-Q01 only the parameters this page declares reach the typed query

mutants.note: an out-of-range page size is clamped instead of refused
cases: V1-Q07 the page size comes from the offered set, and is never a clamp

mutants.note: a cursor is used without the pinned window it was minted for
cases: V1-Q05 the window is resolved from the range, and a page link pins it

mutants.note: an unbounded, arbitrary cursor string is forwarded
cases: V1-Q06 a cursor is bounded and charset-checked, and otherwise opaque

mutants.note: a filter change keeps the cursor, resuming a walk that no longer exists
cases: V1-Q09 changing a filter drops the cursor; a page link keeps the window

mutants.note: a page link drops the pinned window, so the second page slides with the clock
cases: V1-Q09 changing a filter drops the cursor; a page link keeps the window
V1-V08 the next-page link carries the cursor and pins the window

mutants.note: a metadata-only row is drawn as a capture failure
cases: V1-V01 every content state is its own state, and only a lost capture is a failure
V1-V03 the indicators count projection lag, loss and unfinished rows on this page

mutants.note: a lost capture is not drawn as a loss at all
mutants.find: lost: { label: "Lost", tone: "warn", failed: true, unexpected: false },
mutants.replace: lost: { label: "Lost", tone: "warn", failed: false, unexpected: false },
cases: V1-V01 every content state is its own state, and only a lost capture is a failure
V1-V02 a lost row names its reason, and a lost row with no reason says exactly that
V1-V03 the indicators count projection lag, loss and unfinished rows on this page

mutants.note: an off row in the list passes as an ordinary state instead of a projection defect
cases: V1-V01 every content state is its own state, and only a lost capture is a failure
V1-V03 the indicators count projection lag, loss and unfinished rows on this page

mutants.note: a row that did not fail borrows the loss reason anyway
cases: V1-V01 every content state is its own state, and only a lost capture is a failure
V1-V03 the indicators count projection lag, loss and unfinished rows on this page

mutants.note: a request with no status yet is drawn as a success
cases: V1-V05 status tone follows the class, and an unset status is not drawn as success

mutants.note: a filtered empty page reads as "no traffic"
cases: V1-V06 an empty page distinguishes filtered, capture-off and simply idle

mutants.note: an organization capturing nothing is told there is simply no traffic
mutants.find: const capturing = context.keys.some((key) => key.trace_mode !== "off" && key.revoked_at === null);
cases: V1-V06 an empty page distinguishes filtered, capture-off and simply idle

mutants.note: a retry is offered for failures retrying cannot fix
cases: V1-V07 an error offers a retry only where retrying can work

mutants.note: any response is applied, so a stale one overwrites the current filters
cases: V1-S02 a response that lost the race cannot put the older filter back
V1-S03 a duplicate delivery of a response already applied changes nothing

mutants.note: a duplicate delivery of an applied response is applied again
cases: V1-S03 a duplicate delivery of a response already applied changes nothing

mutants.note: an arrival that answers an older request is taken as the answer to the newest
mutants.find: if (!same(sequence.query, arrived)) return { sequence, applied: false };
cases: V1-S05 an arrival that does not answer the outstanding request is dropped

mutants.note: the controls draw whatever page arrived, including an older one
mutants.find: return outstanding && sequence.issued > sequence.applied ? sequence.query : arrived;
cases: V1-S06 the controls draw the newest request while one is outstanding
